knowledge_point.title: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 3x3 Matrix

question.:question/problem:
$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 7 & 8\end{bmatrix},\,B=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form $R_{i}:=R_{i}+kR_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below $a_{11}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 7 & 8\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{2}:=R_{2}-2R_{1}}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 7 & 8\end{bmatrix}
\xrightarrow{R_{3}:=R_{3}-3R_{1}}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}=B
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$R_{2}:=R_{2}-2R_{1}$ and $R_{3}:=R_{3}-3R_{1}$.
